resources.string: PC VR on your phone, with 6DoF tracking from the phone\'s own camera.
Tap Start, then put the phone in your headset. In VR, the ✕ (top left) returns here and ⚙ (top right) has quick settings.
Loads your headset\'s lens profile. Use the QR code printed on Cardboard-style viewers.
On the PC\'s hotspot (%1$s). Best latency.
On Wi-Fi (%1$s). A PC hotspot on 5 GHz gives lower latency.
Not on Wi-Fi. Join the same network as your PC (ideally its Windows Mobile hotspot).
Google Play Services for AR needs installing or updating. Tap to install.
This phone doesn\'t support ARCore. You\'ll get rotation-only (3DoF) tracking.
Needed for 6DoF and hand tracking. Tap to grant.

The phone broadcasts on the network and the PC finds it.
Also contacts this PC directly. Use it if the PC never sees the phone, e.g. on guest Wi-Fi, through a VPN, or on routers that block broadcasts.
This phone: IP %1$s, ALVR name %2$s.\n\nIf the PC still doesn\'t list the phone, add it in the ALVR dashboard under Devices → Add device manually, with this name and IP.
Phone PCVR can use the camera for 6DoF and hand tracking. You can revoke this in the app\'s permissions.
The camera is needed for 6DoF and hand tracking. Without it you get rotation-only (3DoF) tracking. If Grant does nothing, allow it in the app\'s permissions.
Status: %1$s\n\n6DoF uses Google Play Services for AR to track the phone\'s position from the rear camera. Turn it off for rotation-only tracking, for example in a dark room.

On the PC, run ALVR Streamer v20.8.0 (other versions won't connect) and launch SteamVR from its dashboard.

This phone shows up as %1$s (IP %2$s). Press Trust next to it the first time.

If it never appears, check Network settings.
Run ALVR Streamer v20.8.0 on your PC and press Trust on this phone the first time it appears. Tap for this phone\'s name and help.
Lean and walk using the rear camera (ARCore). Off = rotation only.
Re-projects frames to your latest head rotation. Cuts perceived lag when turning.
Uses the camera to track your hands as controllers. Pinch = trigger, fist = grip. Unreliable for now.
Forces full screen brightness while streaming.
Shows tracking numbers inside each eye.
Line the two pictures up with your headset\'s lenses and your eyes. Changes apply live, even while streaming.
Distance between the two pictures. Match your headset\'s lens spacing: if you see double or straining, change this first.
Makes each eye\'s picture bigger or smaller (magnification).
How far the picture reaches towards the edges. Lower it if the edges look cut off or stretched.
Moves both pictures up or down to the lens centres.
How far apart the game\'s cameras are, without moving the pictures. More = the world looks smaller and deeper.

While streaming:
• Tap Vol + / Vol − : volume
• Hold Vol + : headset fit
• Hold Vol − : SteamVR menu
• Tap both : reset play space
• Hold both : gaze pointer on / off
With Gaze pointer on: Vol − is the trigger (tap = click, hold = drag) and tap Vol + opens the SteamVR menu.
In headset fit: tap = change, hold Vol + = next, hold Vol − = back, tap both = save.

A laser that follows where you look, as your right controller. In VR: hold both volume keys to turn it on or off. While on, Vol − = trigger (tap = click, hold = drag) and tap Vol + = SteamVR menu. Replaces the right tracked hand while on.

GAZE POINTER ON

Tap Vol + SteamVR menu
Vol − click (hold = drag)
Hold Vol + laser angle
STEAMVR MENU\n\nVol − click · Hold Vol + laser angle
Tilts the gaze laser up or down if its dot isn\'t where you\'re looking.

Tap Vol + / Vol − change
Hold Vol + %5$s · Hold Vol − back

Makes where you are and the way you\'re facing the centre and forward of the play space. In VR: tap both volume keys together, or ⚙ → Reset play space.
In VR: hold Vol − to open or close the SteamVR menu (the dashboard and in-game overlays like VRChat\'s).
Reset queued: it happens a few seconds after you next tap Start VR, so face forward once the headset is on.
Reset play space on every start
A few seconds after the stream screen opens, wherever you\'re facing becomes forward.

• Play seated and move with a keyboard or gamepad. Head tracking is the strong part.
• Keep the rear camera uncovered, and play in a lit room with some visible detail.
• On Windows, turn on Mobile hotspot (5 GHz) and join it from the phone instead of using a router.
• Slow, smooth head movement tracks best.

Phone PCVR streams SteamVR games from your PC to your phone, with 6DoF head tracking, timewarp and experimental hand tracking computed on the phone.\n\nIt\'s free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0, and it\'s built on the open-source projects below. Thank you to everyone who made them.

Camera permission is needed for 6DoF tracking. Running rotation-only (3DoF).
Storage access is needed to load your headset\'s lens profile.
Phone PCVR crashed last time. Tap to view the log.
If the stream falls badly behind (frames arriving seconds late), shows a steady head-tracked room with an explanation instead of a lagging world.
Tells you when 6DoF pauses (too dark, too little detail, hand too close) or the stream falls behind, so nothing looks random.
Stream %.1f s behind. Paused for comfort.
6DoF paused: too dark for the camera. Turn on a light.
6DoF paused: the camera sees too little detail. Face furniture or a textured area.
6DoF paused: moving too fast for the camera.
6DoF paused: camera tracking lost. Rotation only.
6DoF paused: hand too close to the camera.
Pick the profile that matches your setup. Each option can also be switched in VR (⚙ → Latency & picture) to compare.
Lowest latency. Shows the newest frame right away. Pair with the low-end PC streamer profile (lower resolution and bitrate).
Smoothest on a weak link. Keeps one spare frame, freezes instead of smearing when a frame is lost, and limits prediction during lag spikes.
You changed an option by hand.
Draws each frame just before the screen refreshes instead of several frames ahead. Biggest cut in screen delay.
Shows the newest decoded frame and skips older queued ones. Lower latency; a jittery link may look less smooth.
After a lost frame, keeps showing the last good picture (still head-tracked) until a clean keyframe arrives, instead of blocky smears.
Caps how far ahead your head is predicted when the network spikes, so the view stops running ahead of you.
Aims timewarp at the screen delay this phone actually measures, instead of a fixed guess.
Predicts less while a head turn slows down, so the view does not swing past where you stopped.
Where timewarp runs out of picture, repeat the edge instead of showing black.
Spare decoded frames kept waiting when Newest frame only is off. 1 smooths a jittery link for about 16 ms more latency. PC setting = ALVR\'s own logic.
How long a frame may wait for the video decoder before it is dropped. Dropping one corrupts the picture until the next keyframe.
Most look-ahead allowed when Limit prediction during lag is on.
How far ahead head position may be extrapolated. Lower = less overshoot when you stop moving.
The PC renders this much extra on every edge, so timewarp turns into real picture instead of black. Costs a little sharpness.
How much of the screen delay timewarp predicts ahead. Lower if turns feel like they run ahead.
How long before the refresh drawing starts (with frame pacing). Raise if the overlay shows render below 60 Hz.
Also shifts the picture when you walk, lean or tilt, at display time, instead of waiting for the next PC frame. Assumes the scene is about one distance away (below).
With hand tracking on, the app opens the camera itself and gives hands a sharper stream of their own, instead of ARCore\'s small image. Applies the next time VR starts.
Pinch = trigger, fist = grip, decided on the phone with a firm threshold and a short delay, so a relaxed hand doesn\'t click. Turn off ALVR\'s own gestures on the PC so they don\'t fire as well.

Run hand tracking on your PC instead of the phone: faster and steadier on older phones. Start pc_assist on the PC (pc-assist folder); the phone sends its hand camera as JPEG over Wi-Fi (about 5-12 Mbit/s). Without the PC app the phone tracks hands itself.
Send the hand camera to the PC as H.264 from the phone\'s hardware encoder (about 4 Mbit/s) instead of JPEG pictures (about 12 Mbit/s). Off = JPEG.
Wi-Fi used by the hand camera in H.264 mode. Higher = sharper fingers for the PC, more Wi-Fi.
JPEG quality of the camera frames sent to the PC. Lower = less Wi-Fi traffic, slightly less precise fingers.
Pinch and hold with your left hand, then move the hand: that\'s the left thumbstick, relative to where you face. Let go to stop. A quick left pinch without moving is still a click.
How far the hand must move from the pinch point before you start moving.
Hand distance from the pinch point for full stick tilt.
Tracking one hand only is faster (MediaPipe stops looking for a second hand) and that hand can never be mistaken for the other one.
Thumb-to-index distance (centre to centre) that counts as a click. Lower = needs a firmer pinch.
Distance at which the click lets go. Keep well above the click distance.
How closed the fist must be to grab (fingertips to palm). Lower = tighter fist.
How open the hand must be to let go.
How far away positional timewarp assumes things are. Lower if nearby objects swim when you move, higher if the distance does.
Profile set. It applies right away; resolution changes need the PC streamer profile.
